title: Where you are signed in
purpose: See the browsers where your account is signed in now and sign out the ones you do not recognize or no longer use.
summary: The browsers where your account is signed in now, with when each signed in and was last active. Sign out any you do not recognize or no longer use.

tasks.title: Sign out a browser you no longer use
steps: Find the row by its browser, address and times.
Select [[Sign out]] on that row, then confirm. That browser goes to the sign-in page at its next request.

tasks.title: Sign out everywhere except here
steps: Select [[Sign out of all other sessions]] and confirm.
The message says how many were signed out, including any that signed in after you opened the page.

tasks.title: Check that nobody else is using your account
steps: Look for a browser, address or sign-in time you do not recognize. Sign it out, then change your password from the account menu.

good_to_know: Signing out a session does not stop anyone signing in again. If you think someone else knows your password, change it: that ends your other sessions too.
Anything typed and not saved in a browser you sign out is lost.
The browser name and the address are what each browser and the network reported at sign-in, so they can be wrong.
A session also leaves the list when it passes the laboratory's session limits or is signed out there.
On a shared demonstration account you see only your own session: the others belong to other visitors.

sections.title: Who can use this page
paragraphs: Every signed-in account, staff or client portal, opens it from the account menu (Where you are signed in). It shows only your own account's sessions; nobody else's sessions are listed, and a superuser in the admin console sees only how many of your sessions are open, not their times, browsers or addresses.

A shared demonstration account, one whose password the deployment publishes on the sign-in page, sees only the session it is using, a notice with how many other sessions are open, and no Sign out buttons: the other sessions are other visitors', so they cannot be listed or signed out here.

items.label: Browser
items.description: The browser and system, such as Firefox on Windows, worked out from how the browser described itself when the session signed in. Unknown browser when it gave nothing recognizable. This browser marks the session you are using now; it is always listed first.

items.label: Address at sign-in
items.description: The network address the session signed in from, as the deployment reports it. Behind a proxy the deployment must be told which proxy to trust, or every session shows the proxy's address (see Security settings). Not recorded for a session that signed in before this was recorded, or when no address was available.

items.label: Signed in
items.description: When the session signed in, in the laboratory's time zone.

items.label: Last activity
items.description: When the session last opened a page, saved, searched or chose Stay signed in. Reading or typing does not count, and neither do the page's own checks of how long remains.

items.label: Open sessions
items.description: The number in the panel header counts the rows shown.

items.label: Sign out
items.description: On each other session's row. Asks for confirmation, then ends that session; its browser goes to the sign-in page at its next request, with a notice that it was signed out from another session of your account. If the session had already ended (signed out there, past a session limit) nothing changes and the message says so. The session you are using has no button: use Sign out in the account menu.

items.label: Sign out of all other sessions
items.description: In the page header when another session is listed. Asks for confirmation, then ends every other session of your account open at that moment, including any that signed in after you opened the page; the message says how many, and how many of those signed in later. This browser stays signed in.

sections.title: Rules and records
paragraphs: A session is listed while it is open and inside both session limits, measured by the server's clock. A browser that was closed without signing out stays listed until it passes a limit.

Each sign-out from this page is recorded in the audit history with the sessions ended, without their browsers or addresses, and in the sign-in log. A change being saved from the session you sign out at that moment finishes first; one it starts afterwards is refused and that browser is signed out.
If your own session ended while this page was open (it was signed out from another browser, or passed a limit), a sign-out sent from it is refused and you go to the sign-in page.
A session that passes a session limit while it is being signed out is recorded as ended by that limit.
Signing out ends sessions only. It does not change your password, your second factor or your access.
